payload.problem_addressed: Behaviour-cloned (BC) robot policies cannot self-improve from their own failures at deployment time without additional human demonstrations, and RL fine-tuning of multi-billion-parameter VLA policies is expensive and can degrade the BC prior.
payload.method_summary: Q-Planning attaches a small (~1B-parameter) off-policy Q-function, with its own DinoV2/T5 encoders and an HL-Gauss categorical Bellman-loss head over action chunks, to a frozen large BC policy. At inference, N candidate action chunks are drawn from the frozen BC policy and combined via a single-step softmax Q-weighted average (no iterative search). During deployment, both successful and failed rollouts are appended to a replay buffer and used to fine-tune only the Q-function (BC weights never updated), closing a self-improvement loop.
payload.contributions_summary: The paper introduces Q-Planning, which equips a frozen large visuomotor BC policy with a small off-policy Q-function that can be trained on both successful and failed rollouts (an asymmetry BC lacks). It combines a real-time Q-weighted action selector over BC draws with an online self-improvement loop that updates only the Q-function. Across LIBERO, bimanual RoboTwin, and two real-robot contact-rich tasks, ten iterations of self-improvement lift every benchmark tested (e.g., RoboTwin 83.8%->91.4%, real-robot stack-cups 40%->90%), and it is shown to be the only method among five online baselines (Best-of-N, filtered SFT, IBRL, DSRL, DAWR) that improves stably from failures without training an auxiliary actor.
key_architecture_choices: Frozen large BC policy (FastWAM) as the action-proposal distribution; only a small (~1B param) auxiliary Q-function is trained/updated

Q-function has parameter-disjoint DinoV2 (visual) and T5 (language) encoders from the BC policy, feeding a transformer decoder that cross-attends to those tokens and takes the candidate action chunk as query tokens
HL-Gauss categorical regression (101 bins) instead of scalar MSE Bellman regression, for stability under sparse/bimodal terminal rewards
Q-chunking: treats the length-H action chunk as a single super-action to shrink the effective bootstrapping horizon by a factor of H
Inference-time action selection is a single-step softmax Q-weighted average over N multi-modal flow-matching draws (3-step truncated denoising) rather than iterative sample-based search (e.g., MPPI)
Bootstrap target uses the next buffer chunk directly (one-step-shifted target) rather than a planner-selected action, avoiding an extra planner call per Bellman update
datasets: Real-robot: stack-cups and insert-wallet (bimanual YAM arms, 100 base demos each)
payload.headline_results: Ten iterations of Q-only self-improvement lift mean success across LIBERO+RoboTwin from 92.1% to 97.6% (+5.5pp over frozen BC); on real-robot contact-rich tasks, five iterations lift stack-cups 40%->90% and insert-wallet 25%->80%, while SFT on successes alone stalls at 55%/30%. Under an identical online budget, Q-Planning is the only tested method (vs. Best-of-N, filtered SFT, IBRL, DSRL, DAWR) that improves stably from failures without an auxiliary actor.
claimed_advantages: Self-improves from both successful and failed deployment rollouts without ever updating the (multi-billion-parameter) BC policy weights, so cost scales with the small critic rather than the policy
Real-time: a full planning step (N=32, RoboTwin) takes 400ms, comfortably inside the 960ms replan budget and 1.6x faster than a single 10-step BC inference
No auxiliary actor is trained (unlike IBRL/DSRL), and it is plug-and-play with a large pretrained VLA policy
limitations: Cannot bootstrap from scratch: any behavior the frozen BC head cannot produce with non-negligible probability is unreachable by the planner/loop
The Q-decoder cost scales linearly with candidate count N, so pushing N into the hundreds would eventually make Q-scoring the latency bottleneck
Assumes a per-episode success detector (environment success bit in sim, human-provided label on the real robot); open-ended tasks would need a learned success model
payload.applicability_to_our_problem: Directly transferable pattern for hexgen's self-play/verifier-in-the-loop and value/critic-guided search live problems: instead of (or alongside) resampling best-of-N candidates purely by rerunning the frozen verifier, train a small auxiliary value/critic head (analogous scale to hexgen's own ~27M decoder) that scores candidate programs/program-prefixes, is trained on both verifier-pass and verifier-fail rollouts, and is periodically refreshed from deployment while the main graph-transformer decoder stays frozen -- giving cheap, decoupled self-improvement from the verifier's pass/fail signal without expensive full-model RL. The single-step softmax-weighted aggregation over multiple decoder draws (rather than iterative MCTS/beam search) is also a cheap alternative worth considering for combining best-of-N program candidates at inference.
payload.reviewer_notes: This is a robotics/VLA paper, not CAD or program synthesis, so the applicability is a structural/methodological analogy rather than a direct technique transfer. The core insight -- decouple a frozen generator from a small trainable critic that can learn from failures the generator itself cannot be trained on -- maps well onto hexgen's frozen-verifier + best-of-N sampling setup, where the verifier already supplies a natural pass/fail (and possibly graded) reward signal that could train such a critic over program prefixes for value-guided beam/MCTS search (a live problem #1 item explicitly named in our problem statement).
dependencies_on_other_methods: HL-Gauss categorical value regression (Farebrother et al. 2024)

payload.problem_addressed: Vanilla GRPO post-training for semantic-ID (SID) generative recommendation is poorly matched to the tree-structured, hierarchical output space: when the current policy's rollout group misses the target SID branch entirely (target-missing prompts), item-level rewards can collapse to identical/near-identical values across the group, producing weak or degenerate GRPO advantage signal exactly where post-training should matter most.
payload.method_summary: DASO profiles each on-policy rollout group by prefix-match depth against the target SID (an M-level tree) to locate the bottleneck depth where candidates most often leave the target path, then deterministically reallocates a bounded, monotonically-sized subset of the group to prefix-guided completions (forcing the correct prefix up to the bottleneck depth and letting the policy decode the rest) while retaining the strongest raw rollouts for GRPO contrast. A graded SID-prefix reward (fraction of matched depth) supplements the binary/ranking reward, and a token-level SFT anchor loss on the ground-truth SID is added to limit regression on prompts the SFT checkpoint already solves.
payload.contributions_summary: The paper diagnoses that under a frozen SFT checkpoint, the top-16 beam-decoded candidates miss the target item's first SID token for 52.5-63.9% of test prompts, causing degenerate GRPO reward variation. It introduces DASO, a tree-aware GRPO post-training method combining online prefix-depth profiling, bottleneck-aware bounded rollout reallocation, a graded SID-prefix reward, and SFT-anchored stabilization. DASO improves over MiniOneRec-style GRPO on 11 of 12 public-benchmark metrics (best on 9 of 12) across two Amazon categories and two Qwen backbone sizes, and improves most level-wise recall metrics on an internal four-level industrial SID task, with the largest gains concentrated on initially partial-prefix and no-prefix ('Hard'/'Medium') prompts.
key_architecture_choices: Cumulative prefix-depth profile p_j(x) over an M-level SID tree, computed online from the current policy's raw rollout group each RL step (not fixed offline difficulty buckets)

Deterministic, monotone guided-budget rule B(x): more guided slots when the group's average prefix-match depth is smaller, bounded by B_max (=9), with zero intervention once the group already contains an exact target-SID hit
Guided slots allocated across tree depths in proportion to the profile 'drops' (fraction of rollouts that match through depth j-1 but fail at depth j), using largest-remainder rounding

Guided completions fix the target prefix up to the bottleneck depth and let the current policy sample only the remaining suffix; GRPO likelihood-ratio terms apply only to the policy-generated suffix tokens (forced prefix is conditioning context, not a sampled action)
Weakest raw rollouts (by prefix-match depth) are the ones replaced by guided completions, preserving the strongest raw on-policy rollouts for GRPO's group-relative contrast
Graded SID-prefix reward R_sid = matched-depth / M added (unit weight) to the existing binary item-hit + ranking reward
Auxiliary token-level SFT loss on the ground-truth SID sequence added to the GRPO loss (lambda_sft = 0.1) to limit distribution shift/regression from the guided rollouts
datasets: Amazon Reviews 2018: Industrial and Scientific; Office Products (5-core chronological next-item)
Internal industrial user-to-item recommendation dataset (1.36M examples, 319K users, four-level SIDs)
payload.headline_results: DASO improves over MiniOneRec-style GRPO on 11/12 public metrics (best on 9/12); e.g. Office Products HR@5 rises from 0.1420->0.1639 (1.5B) and 0.1313->0.1683 (3B). On the internal 4-level SID task, first-level Top-20 recall rises from 47.21% to 54.23% and final-level (lv3) recall from 4.23% to 4.67%, with Top-1 recall improved at all four levels.
claimed_advantages: Recovers useful reward contrast specifically on target-missing (partial-prefix/no-prefix) prompts, where vanilla item-level GRPO reward collapses to near-degenerate variation
Deterministic, group-local, requires no extra learned value/allocator model (in contrast to approaches needing a learned value or search module)
SFT anchor empirically mitigates the regression that guided rollouts would otherwise cause on prompts the SFT checkpoint already solves (removing it drops aggregate HR@5 by ~2-3pp in ablations)
limitations: Comparisons against MiniOneRec+GT and Sibling-GRPO combine multiple DASO components at once, so gains are not attributable to the allocation rule alone
One exception where the GRPO baseline slightly outperforms DASO on an intermediate metric (internal Top-20 lv2)
Reported public-benchmark numbers are from single runs (no reported variance/seeds)
payload.applicability_to_our_problem: The core mechanism -- diagnose exactly where in a partially-generated structured/tree output a policy's rollouts diverge from a valid target, then spend a bounded, prefix-conditioned repair budget concentrated at that bottleneck depth while keeping the rest of the rollout group on-policy -- is a close analog to hexgen's structural-validity live problem #1 (DAgger-style repair/edit distillation for broken autoregressive rollouts). Hexgen could similarly profile where best-of-N program rollouts first diverge from compiling/verifier-passing continuations (e.g., which DSL command position first goes wrong), then allocate repair-guided completions (teacher-forcing the correct prefix up to that command) concentrated there, while preserving raw on-policy rollouts as contrast for an RL/GRPO-style update -- rather than either uniform ground-truth injection or ignoring the failure-location signal entirely. The graded partial-credit reward (matched-prefix-depth / total-depth) is also directly reusable as a shaping signal for partially-valid but not-yet-compiling programs.
payload.reviewer_notes: Domain is generative recommendation (semantic-ID retrieval), not program/CAD synthesis, so this is a methodological transfer, not a technique with released CAD-relevant code. The 'prefix-depth bottleneck profiling + bounded guided reallocation' idea generalizes naturally to any tree/sequence-structured autoregressive generation task with a verifiable/checkable target structure, which includes hexgen's DSL programs (command sequence with a well-defined 'first point of divergence' concept, analogous to prefix-match depth here). Code released at https://github.com/LucasXinYu/DASO.
dependencies_on_other_methods: MiniOneRec pipeline (SID construction via RQ-VAE, SFT, constrained decoding, GRPO reward)

payload.impact_rationale: A plausible but unproven route to a self-improving critic layered on our frozen decoder+verifier, but it requires domain-specific redesign to move from continuous robot actions to discrete DSL program tokens.
payload.effort_rationale: Needs a new auxiliary critic network, replay-buffer infrastructure for verifier-pass/fail rollouts, and integration of Q-weighted aggregation into best-of-N program decoding -- a multi-week project.

payload.impact_rationale: Prefix-depth bottleneck profiling plus a graded partial-credit reward directly targets our structural-validity problem: best-of-N program rollouts diverging from verifier-passing continuations early in the DSL sequence.
payload.effort_rationale: Requires a GRPO-style RL training loop, prefix-depth profiling over DSL command sequences, and a bounded guided-rollout mechanism -- moderate engineering on top of existing best-of-N + verifier infrastructure.
